# Euno Shadowing

> Free accent practice by shadowing a speaker you choose. Euno compares your recording with their audio and marks the sounds that differ (English, beta, no score), plus your timing and melody.

Euno Shadowing is a free web app for accent practice. Cut a short clip from a video of someone whose accent you want, speak along with it for fifteen minutes, and Euno compares your recording with the speaker’s audio and marks the sounds that differ.

## What it is, and what it is not

- Cost: Euno Shadowing is completely free. There is no subscription, no paid plan or premium tier, no free trial (there is nothing to subscribe to) and no card to enter. Only the optional Ask Euno feature can cost money, because it uses the user's own AI key and the provider bills them directly.
- Euno Shadowing is a free web app at shadowing.euno.cc for practising pronunciation and accent by shadowing (speaking along with a recording) in English, French and Spanish. Full explanation: https://shadowing.euno.cc/what-is-euno-shadowing/
- You bring your own videos or audio (upload a file or paste a link to an .mp4) and cut short clips of one or two sentences. There are no built-in lessons, no content library, no subtitles and no transcripts, and it does not pull content from YouTube (a direct link must point to an .mp4 file; YouTube links do not work).
- Cost and sign-in: free, with no subscription, no paid tier and no ads. Sign-in is with a Google account (no card). The only cost is optional AI use, billed by the provider whose API key the user supplies.
- It is not an app for job shadowing (such as Erasmus+ visits for teachers), medical or pre-med shadowing, or the Euno enterprise AI platform, and is not affiliated with them. It is also not the journaling apps named Euno.
- Core idea: you pick a speaker and clips, shadow them, and Euno compares your recording with the speaker's actual audio. For English clips it marks where your sounds differ from the speaker's (a Pronunciation tab, beta); for every language it also shows your timing and melody next to the speaker's.
- Pronunciation feedback (English only, beta, off by default): after a recorded pass, the Pronunciation tab compares the sounds in your recording with the sounds in the speaker's audio and marks up to three places where yours differ, with the words they fall in. It shows differences from the speaker, not mistakes. It compares against the speaker's actual audio, not a transcript or a standard accent, and gives no score. It does not coach tongue or lip position. The analysis runs in the browser on a computer after a one-time download of a speech model of about 71 MB from Hugging Face, and the recording is not uploaded for it. It can misread a sound, and it shows nothing when the audio is too noisy. The words shown above the sounds come from a separate optional speech model, Whisper, about 80 MB, also downloaded once and run in the browser, because clips have no transcripts. Across sessions Euno keeps a history of which sound differences keep coming back and which have gone quiet. French and Spanish clips do not have the sound comparison yet; they get timing and melody.
- Other feedback: how far behind or ahead of the speaker you were, where you went faster or slower, and pitch direction and stress, after each recorded pass. An optional speech-recognition check (Chrome only, off by default) can mark clip words that may have been unclear. Ask Euno (optional, with your own Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter key) answers questions about notes and measurements; only text is sent, never audio.
- No score and no grade anywhere. Euno does not claim to be a pronunciation scoring tool like ELSA Speak: it compares you with the speaker you chose.

## Features

- English pronunciation feedback: marks the sounds that differ from the speaker’s audio, analysed in your browser (beta, no score)
- Guided four-step shadowing sessions on clips cut from your own videos
- Pronunciation history across sessions: which differences keep coming back
- Timing and melody comparison with the speaker
- Recording and side-by-side playback
- Ask Euno: questions and notes answered with your own AI key (optional)
- 12-week check-ins against a baseline
- Discord and push practice reminders
- Optional read-only connection to Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini through MCP (sign-in required), so an AI app can see the user's own practice data, including the pronunciation history (tools get_pronunciation_progress and get_clip_pronunciation: the speaker's and the learner's sounds per clip and per take, English only, compared with the speaker's audio). It cannot change anything and never receives audio
- Clips cut from your own videos, with a zoomed waveform for trimming at the pauses
- Looping, playback at 0.5x, 0.75x or 1x, and keyboard shortcuts
- A five-minute bad-day version of the session; durations and pass counts are settings

- [What is Euno Shadowing? What it does and does not do](https://shadowing.euno.cc/what-is-euno-shadowing/): Euno Shadowing is a free web app for practising accent by shadowing your own videos. What it does, what it does not do (no lessons, subtitles or transcripts), and how it differs from similarly named things.
- [What is shadowing? How the technique works for pronunciation](https://shadowing.euno.cc/what-is-shadowing/): Shadowing is speaking along with a recording at the same time as the speaker. Learn how it works, why it improves rhythm and intonation, and how to start.
- [How long does shadowing take to improve your accent?](https://shadowing.euno.cc/how-long-does-shadowing-take/): What to expect from daily shadowing practice: what changes first, what takes longer, and how to tell whether your accent is really moving.
- [How to choose speakers and clips for shadowing](https://shadowing.euno.cc/choosing-shadowing-clips/): What makes a good shadowing clip: the right speaker, natural speech, clear audio, the right length and where to cut. With a checklist.
- [Shadowing vs listen and repeat, minimal pairs and reading aloud](https://shadowing.euno.cc/shadowing-vs-other-methods/): How shadowing compares with listen-and-repeat, minimal pairs, reading aloud and learning phonetics, what each is good for, and how to combine them.
- [Euno Shadowing vs ELSA Speak and Language Reactor](https://shadowing.euno.cc/euno-vs-elsa-and-language-reactor/): An honest comparison of Euno Shadowing, ELSA Speak and Language Reactor: what each tool is for, what it does not do, and how to choose or combine them.
- [Euno Shadowing vs Shadow Talk and Praat](https://shadowing.euno.cc/euno-vs-shadow-talk-and-praat/): An honest comparison of Euno Shadowing, Shadow Talk and Praat: what each tool is for, what it does not do, and how to choose or combine them.
- [How to improve your English accent with shadowing: a daily routine](https://shadowing.euno.cc/accent-shadowing/): A practical 15-minute daily shadowing routine for your English accent: choosing clips, the four steps, recording yourself and measuring progress over 12 weeks.
- [Which English accent to shadow: American, British or Australian?](https://shadowing.euno.cc/english-accents/): General American, Southern British and General Australian compared for shadowing: the features to listen for, and how to choose one to practise.
- [How to improve your French accent with shadowing: a daily routine](https://shadowing.euno.cc/french-accent-shadowing/): A 15-minute daily shadowing routine for your French accent: French rhythm, liaison and linking, vowels, nasal vowels and the French “r”, and how to track progress.
- [Parisian or Québécois French: which accent to shadow?](https://shadowing.euno.cc/french-accents/): Metropolitan (Parisian) and Québécois French compared for shadowing: the main differences in vowels, consonants and melody, and how to choose.
- [How to improve your Spanish accent with shadowing: a daily routine](https://shadowing.euno.cc/spanish-accent-shadowing/): A 15-minute daily shadowing routine for your Spanish accent: Spanish rhythm, the five vowels, “r” and “rr”, soft b, d and g, linking, and tracking progress.
- [Mexican, Spain or Argentine Spanish: which accent to shadow?](https://shadowing.euno.cc/spanish-accents/): Mexican, Peninsular (Spain) and Rioplatense Spanish compared for shadowing: the sounds that set each apart, and how to choose one to practise.

## Facts

- What is shadowing? Shadowing means speaking along with a recording at the same time as the speaker, copying their rhythm, melody and sounds as closely as you can. It trains the way you speak, not just the way you understand.
- What is Euno Shadowing, and is it related to job shadowing or Euno AI? Euno Shadowing is a free web app for practising your accent by shadowing: speaking along with short clips of videos you bring. After a recorded pass it compares your recording with the speaker’s audio and, for English, marks the sounds that differ. It also shows your timing and melody next to theirs. It is not related to job-shadowing programmes such as Erasmus+, to medical shadowing, or to the Euno enterprise AI platform. What it is, and what it is not.
- Can it correct my pronunciation? In part, and only for English. After a recorded pass, the Pronunciation tab compares the sounds in your recording with the sounds in the speaker’s audio and marks up to three places where yours differ, with the words they fall in. It shows differences from the speaker, not mistakes: it compares you with the speaker you chose, not with a transcript or a standard accent, and it gives no score. It does not coach where to put your tongue or lips. It is a beta feature and it can misread a sound, so each item can be dismissed with “Sounds the same to me”. It runs in your browser, on a computer: it is off until you turn it on in Settings → Analysis, which downloads a speech model of about 71 MB to your device once (from Hugging Face, a third-party host), and your recording is not uploaded for it. French and Spanish clips get the timing and melody measurements only, for now.
- What feedback does it give? For English, the Pronunciation tab marks up to three places per recorded pass where your sounds differ from the speaker’s audio (beta, off by default, no score). For every language, Euno also shows how far behind or ahead of the speaker you were, where you went faster or slower, and where your pitch and stress went another way. You can play the original and your recording one after the other or together. An optional speech-recognition check (Chrome only, off by default) can mark words that may have been unclear. Ask Euno, with your own AI key, can answer questions about your notes and these measurements. Euno gives no score, and it has no automatic subtitles or transcripts.
- Does it cost anything? No. Euno Shadowing is completely free: there is no subscription, no paid plan, no premium tier and no card to enter, and no ads. The only thing that can cost money is the optional Ask Euno feature, which uses your own AI key, so any usage is billed to you directly by the provider you pick (Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter). Everything else works without it.
- Is there a free trial or a paid plan? No. There is no free trial because there is nothing to subscribe to: every feature of the app is free from the start, and there are no paid tiers. You can start by signing in with Google.
- Which languages and accents does it support? You can practise English (General Australian, General American or Southern British), French (Parisian or Québécois) or Spanish (Mexican, Spain or Rioplatense), or name another accent of those languages. The app itself is available in English, French and Spanish. More languages, such as Japanese and German, are planned. The sound-level Pronunciation tab is English only for now.
- Where are my videos and recordings stored? In your own Google Drive. When you connect it, the app puts your files in a “Euno Shadowing” folder there, so they’re on every device you sign in on, and it can only see the files it creates. Your browser also keeps a copy of the files you open so they play instantly. Our server only keeps your practice notes and progress, never the audio or video.
- Which videos can I use? Any video or audio file you have the right to use for your own practice: upload a file from your device or paste a direct link to an .mp4. Interviews, podcasts and talks with one clear speaker work best.
- Can I paste a YouTube link? No. Euno does not fetch videos from YouTube or other sites. You need a file you have the right to use, either uploaded from your device or a direct link to an .mp4. If you want to practise with a YouTube video, a browser extension such as Language Reactor works on the page itself; Euno is for cutting a clip from a file you have and comparing your voice with the speaker’s.
- Does Euno come with lessons, videos or transcripts? No. You shadow your own videos: upload a file from your device or paste a direct link to an .mp4 (not a YouTube link), then cut the clips you want to practise. Euno has no lesson library, subtitles or transcripts of its own. It runs the shadowing routine on your clips and compares your voice with the speaker’s.
- Do I need an AI key? No. Everything works without one. With a key from Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter, you can ask Euno about a sound, your notes or your practice inside the app. Without a key, notes give you a prompt to paste into any chatbot.
- Can I connect Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini? Yes, optionally. In Settings → Connections you can link Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini to your own practice data through MCP. They can read your notes, sessions and pronunciation history, and nothing else: they cannot change anything and never receive audio.
- Do I need a microphone? Yes, for recording passes and check-ins. A headset or earphones help, so the speaker’s voice doesn’t leak into your recording.
